briefing.text: On News, Information Technology still leads with buzz 85.0 (down 2.3 on the day, up 2.5 on the week), mentions down 5% and sentiment -0.2, driven by NVDA, MSFT, AMD, AVGO and MU. Financials fell furthest on News (buzz -4.1 to 78.2, though still +11.6 on the week; BAC, UBS, MS, GS, JPM), followed by Materials (buzz -3.5, mentions down 30%). On X, Healthcare buzz jumped 30.6 to 68.4 (mentions up 2,400% from a tiny base; MEDS, WWB) while Technology dropped 17.4 on a 50% fall in mentions (sentiment -0.34). On Reddit, Information Technology stays on top at buzz 95.0 with mentions up 34% (NVDA, ANT, AMD, MU), Healthcare buzz rose 17.3 with mentions up 120% and sentiment 0.32 (MEDS, VVVV), and Financial Services rose 8.1.

BJ #1: raised guidance after Q3 and a membership-fee increase; 12 of 21 articles positive, so it does explain the top rank.
BULL #2: coverage of new AI premium features and whether the stock is fully priced; mixed tone (7 positive, 4 negative), partly explains the rank.
SILVER #3: a story that Asia's AI selloff is spilling into gold, silver and US tech; only 2 articles, so news explains little.
GOLD #4: GLD and IAU outflows and doubts about its safe-haven status (5 of 11 articles negative); fits the 3.1% daily drop.
NIKKEI #6: Asian markets sold off (Taiwan -6.2% on Friday, KOSPI -5.2%, Nikkei down about 4.5% intraday, SoftBank -15%); all 4 articles negative, which explains the rank.
DJI #8: the Dow fell at least 1% on all five days of the week, a first since October 2008; this explains the rank.
NDX #9: 74 articles, mostly stock-watch lists naming QQQ, NVIDIA and Micron; 39 negative, consistent with a 5.6% daily drop.
NVDA #14: over 1,000 articles in two days (294 negative) on its earnings versus calls for Jensen Huang's return; huge coverage, though the rank is held back by attention already running high.

BJ ranks first on attention 3.25x normal and X attention 3.38x normal, both at the 100th percentile, plus volume 1.37x normal and a 3.6-sigma move (-5.3% on the day). Webull is second on above-normal attention (1.15x) and a 2.7-sigma fall of 9.1%, with a Kalshi market that resolves soon as its catalyst. Silver is third on attention 1.22x and X attention 1.23x (both near the 98th percentile) but weaker volume (0.54x) and a smaller 1.6-sigma move. None of the top three has an earnings or Fed catalyst except Webull's market resolving.

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
